key_insight: SRHarness shows that agentic symbolic regression improves most when the runtime itself is designed to manage scientific actions, persistent state, and search trajectories—not just when the LLM or tools are upgraded.
engineering_relevance: For computational science systems, this suggests infrastructure choices like state management and trajectory control can materially affect discovery quality, robustness, and symbolic recovery.
method: Composable scientific actions unify raw, transformed, and candidate-derived quantities behind one interface.
Persistent scientific state stores evaluated hypotheses and exposes compact views to the model.
Trajectory lifecycle management handles continuation, branching, restart, and termination during long searches.
evidence_signal: On LLM-SRBench, SRHarness improved both numerical generalization and symbolic recovery, reaching 93.69% symbolic accuracy on LSR-Transform with DeepSeek-v4-flash-0731 and 72.97% on an anonymized variant, outperforming SR-Scientist and Codex under matched backbones.
watch_item: Results are reported on benchmark tasks, so real-world gains may depend on tool design, prompt structure, and how well the harness generalizes to new scientific domains.
paper_title: SRHarness: A Harness for Agentic Symbolic Regression
